title: Needle-felted adder
subtitle: Britain's only native venomous snake, coiled in grey-brown merino with a dorsal zigzag
excerpt: Needle felt a coiled adder about 30 cm long when uncoiled and displayed in a tight coil about 10 cm across. The dorsal zigzag stripe is the defining mark; needle it in dark brown over a pale grey-brown ground after the body is firm.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional British needle-felting practice. Reptile forms, particularly British native species, are a well-established needle-felting subject in UK guild workshops.

glossaryTerms.definition: A dry felting method using barbed needles to lock wool fibres together without heat or water.
Wool drawn into a continuous ribbon; the standard input material for needle-felting.

content.text: is a long, tapering cylinder in pale grey-brown

with a dark brown dorsal zigzag running the full length of the body. The finished coiled display is about 10 cm across. The body is the main structural challenge: it must taper smoothly from the mid-body diameter (about 1 cm) down to a very fine tail and a slightly flattened head. Work the taper by pulling the roving thinner as you near each end during the initial roll.

attrs.title: Needle safety
attrs.body: Stab straight in and out at 90 degrees. Keep the finger guard on the supporting hand at all times.

items.name: Red glass seed beads for eyes
Strong thread and needle for bead eyes

content.text: Roll the grey-brown roving into a long sausage, starting thick in the middle (about 1.2 cm diameter unfelted) and pulling the roving progressively thinner toward each end. The tail end should be very fine. Needle felt along the length of the sausage from the centre outward, turning and rolling it constantly so the body stays round. A snake body that is compressed flat on one side reads as a worm; keep it consistently cylindrical by needling on all sides.

The head end is slightly flattened vertically and has a triangular shape when viewed from above. Needle the head end slightly flat and then pinch and needle the sides to create the triangular outline. Apply a cream or white patch to the underside of the jaw. The head is only marginally wider than the neck in adders, less pronounced than many other snake species, so keep the widening subtle.

Needle thin strips of cream or pale roving along the underside of the body from head to tail. Keep the belly colour in a straight line; any deviation makes the body look twisted. The belly is a distinctive cream-to-white with dark spots in real adders; simplified as a plain cream strip for the felted version.

With the body firm and the belly colour set, needle the dark brown zigzag along the dorsal surface. Work from head to tail, applying small rectangles of dark roving at alternating diagonal angles to create the zigzag pattern. Each 'tooth' of the zigzag is about 1 cm wide and 5 mm deep on a full-size body. Step back frequently to check the spacing; the zigzag should be consistent along the full length, narrowing as the tail tapers.

Needle a very thin strip of red roving from the tip of the snout, leaving a small forked tip projecting free. Stitch red glass bead eyes into the head just above and slightly behind the jaw line. Adder eyes are set high on the head; do not place them too far forward. Coil the finished snake into a natural resting position and photograph from above to check the zigzag pattern reads clearly.

items.problem: The body is lumpy rather than smooth-cylindrical
items.cause: The needle work was concentrated on one surface, flattening that side while the opposite side remained rounded
items.fix: Roll the body constantly while needling, like rolling a piece of dough, so each face of the cylinder receives equal work. Angled strokes are the enemy of a smooth snake body.

items.problem: The zigzag stripe looks blurry rather than crisp
items.cause: Dark roving fibres spread beyond their needling points because the underlying body was too soft when the stripe was applied
items.fix: Ensure the body is very firm before applying the stripe. Use the size-40 needle for the stripe edges and needle the perimeter of each dark patch tight before moving to the next.
